headline: Approved $2,500,000 settlement from Free Cash and $3,143,557 bond for Poplar Street Pump Station; referred AI ordinance and upzoning overlay district.
summary: The meeting approved a $2,500,000 settlement and a $3,143,557 bond for the Poplar Street Pump Station. Several resolutions on artificial intelligence, school roofs, and sewer overflows were approved. The artificial intelligence ordinance and the Upzoning Overlay district proposal were referred to committees.
decisions: Referred to the Legislative Matters Committee a proposal to amend Section 7.64 on condominium conversions.
Approved and sent to the Public Health and Public Safety Committee a resolution requesting support for local businesses damaged by recent fires.
Referred to the Legislative Matters Committee an ordinance to adopt the Artificial Intelligence Ordinance.
Approved and sent to the School Building Facilities and Maintenance Committee an order asking for a report on the West Somerville Neighborhood School roof.
Approved and sent to the School Building Facilities and Maintenance Committee a resolution asking for a risk-based review of roof drainage and building-envelope components at city schools.
Approved a resolution supporting the Artificial Intelligence Civil Rights Act of 2025.
Approved a resolution calling on the Mayor to adopt policies limiting city use of artificial intelligence.
Approved a resolution asking the Administration to develop or update a severe-weather protocol for construction and roof repair projects.
Approved a resolution urging the state to protect Mass Save and clean energy grants.
Placed on file and sent to the Finance Committee a communication sharing the UASI fiscal year 2024 plan and allocations.
Approved a resolution asking the Director of Mobility to install a SLOW - CHILDREN CROSSING sign on Heath Street.
Approved, by a 9-1 roll call vote, a resolution opposing the draft combined sewer overflows long-term control plan and calling for a regional solution. Wheeler voted no; Strezo was absent.
Approved accepting and spending a $35,000 grant from the Mass Department of Mental Health to the Police Department.
Approved appropriating $100,000 from the Racial and Social Justice Fund for the 2026 Community Grant Cycle.
Approved reducing the borrowing appropriation for the Poplar Street Project by $2,097,667.05.
Approved borrowing $3,143,557 and appropriating the same amount for the Poplar Street Pump Station, by a 10-0 vote with Strezo absent.
Laid on the table a zoning amendment to correct parking maximums.
Laid on the table a zoning amendment to remove ground story elevation requirements.
Laid on the table a zoning amendment to clarify requirements for principal entrances.
Laid on the table a zoning amendment to update terminology for affordable dwelling units and commercial spaces.
Ordained an amendment to Section 1-11(b) of the Code of Ordinances to update enforcement personnel, by a 9-0 vote with Clingan and Strezo absent.
Approved a Grant of Location for Eversource to install 7 feet of conduit in Wheatland Street.
Approved a Grant of Location for Eversource to install 346 feet of conduit in Newton Street.
Referred to the Land Use Committee a zoning amendment to amend use tables and standards.
Referred to the Land Use Committee a zoning amendment to simplify regulation of accessory structures.
Referred to the Land Use Committee a zoning amendment to allow greater adoption of sustainable development elements.
Referred to the Land Use Committee a zoning amendment to simplify regulation of building components.
Referred to the Finance Committee an appropriation of $100,000 from the Encore Artist and Cultural Support Stabilization Fund.

Approved appropriating $2,500,000 from Free Cash to the Judgments & Settlements Account for the settlement of the Nurse, Bonney, and Browne lawsuit, by a 9-1 vote with McLaughlin voting no and Strezo absent.
Approved appropriating $171,922 to fund a collective bargaining agreement with the Firefighters Association of Somerville, Local 76 Union.
Referred to the Finance Committee a supplemental appropriation of $72,824.03 for the two special elections.
Referred to the Finance Committee a transfer of $545,649 to correct an allocation error in the Fiscal Year 2027 budget.
Referred to the Finance Committee a 60-month contract with Boston Carting Services LLC for hauling waste and recycling.
Approved accepting and spending a $25,000 grant from the Barr Foundation for the Community Heat Resilience pilot program.
Approved accepting and spending a $1,776 grant from Somerville Cambridge Elder Services for senior transportation.
Referred to the Finance Committee payment of prior year invoices totaling $12,844.97 for Medicaid billing and collection services.
Approved the Technology-Specific Surveillance Technology Impact Report for Body Worn Cameras.
Approved the Surveillance Technology Impact Report for Body Worn Cameras.
Referred to the Confirmation of Appointments and Personnel Matters Committee the appointment of Gary Rogers to the Condominium Review Board.
Referred to the Confirmation of Appointments and Personnel Matters Committee the appointment of Fatima Climaco to the Condominium Review Board.
Referred to the Licenses and Permits Committee a new garage license for Toucan Auto Center Inc at 619 Somerville Avenue.
Referred to the Land Use Committee an ordinance to establish the Upzoning Overlay (UO) District at Davis Square, Porter Square, and Ball Square.

# City of Somerville, Massachusetts · City Council · Meeting Minutes

Thursday, October 22, 2026 · 7:00 PM

NOTICE: This is NOT the official version of the City Council's minutes. While reasonable efforts have · been made to assure the accuracy of the data provided, do not rely on this information without first · checking with the City Clerk.

## 1. OPENING CEREMONIES

The meeting was called to order at 7:03 PM by Ward Six City Councilor Lance L. Davis. The City Council entered Executive Session at 8:01 PM and returned at 8:38 PM.

1.1. Roll Call

Call of the Roll.

## (ID # 26-1558 )

Councilor Scott arrived at 7:14 PM.

## RESULT: PLACED ON FILE

- Present: Ward Three City Councilor Ben Ewen-Campen
- City Councilor At Large Jon Link
- Ward Two City Councilor Jefferson Thomas (J.T.) Scott
- Ward Four City Councilor Jesse Clingan
- Ward Five City Councilor Naima Sait
- City Councilor At Large Ben Wheeler
- Ward Seven City Councilor Emily Hardt
- Ward One City Councilor Matthew McLaughlin
- City Councilor At Large Wilfred N. Mbah
- Ward Six City Councilor Lance L. Davis

## Absent:

City Councilor At Large Kristen Strezo

1.2. Remembrances Remembrances.

## (ID # 26-1559 )

- Councilors Clingan and McLaughlin requested a moment of silence in
- memory of Patricia A. Galvin Sullivan.

## RESULT: APPROVED

1.3. Minutes

Approval of the Minutes of the Regular Meeting of September 10, 2026.

## (ID # 26-1560 ) RESULT: APPROVED

## 2. CITATIONS

## 3. PUBLIC HEARINGS

## 4. ORDERS, ORDINANCES, RESOLUTIONS AND MOTIONS OF MEMBERS

4.1. Ordinance

By Councilor McLaughlin, Councilor Clingan, Councilor Davis, Councilor

(ID # 26-1551 ) Ewen-Campen, Councilor Hardt, Councilor Link, Councilor Mbah, Councilor Sait, Councilor Scott, Councilor Strezo and Councilor Wheeler

That Section 7.64 of the Code of Ordinances, pertaining to condominium conversions, be amended as detailed within.

Councilor McLaughlin explained that the purpose of this amendment is to strengthen the city’s condominium conversion ordinance by making it clear

that the provisions would still apply in cases where a building is demolished and replaced by condominiums.

## RESULT: REFERRED FOR RECOMMENDATION

FOLLOWUP: Legislative Matters Committee

4.2. Resolution

By Councilor McLaughlin, Councilor Hardt and Councilor Mbah

(ID # 26-1550 ) Requesting support for local businesses damaged by recent fires.

## RESULT: APPROVED AND SENT FOR DISCUSSION

FOLLOWUP: Public Health and Public Safety Committee

4.3. Ordinance

By Councilor Link, Councilor Mbah and Councilor Wheeler

(ID # 26-1557 ) That the City of Somerville adopt the Artificial Intelligence Ordinance as

detailed within.

- Councilor Link expressed concerns about the potential harm artificial

intelligence (AI) could cause to communities and emphasized the need to restrict certain uses. The proposal would not prohibit city staff from using

AI but would require an annual report detailing its use and clear labeling of any AI-generated content.

## RESULT: REFERRED FOR RECOMMENDATION

FOLLOWUP: Legislative Matters Committee

4.4. Order

By Councilor Link, Councilor Hardt, Councilor Mbah and Councilor

(ID # 26-1555 ) Wheeler

- That the Director of Infrastructure and Asset Management report to this City
- Council on the status of the roof at the West Somerville Neighborhood

School, including necessary repairs, what the leak has revealed about the condition of the city’s aging school roofs, and the effectiveness of the continuity of instruction plan.

## RESULT: APPROVED AND SENT FOR DISCUSSION

FOLLOWUP: School Building Facilities and Maintenance Committee

4.5. Resolution

By Councilor Mbah, Councilor Hardt and Councilor Link

(ID # 26-1529 ) That the Commissioner of Public Works conduct a risk-based review of roof

- drainage systems and other vulnerable building-envelope components at city

school facilities, particularly buildings undergoing active roof construction or repairs, and identify any urgent deficiencies requiring immediate

- attention.

## RESULT: APPROVED AND SENT FOR DISCUSSION

FOLLOWUP: School Building Facilities and Maintenance Committee

4.6. Resolution

By Councilor Link, Councilor Ewen-Campen, Councilor Mbah, Councilor

(ID # 26-1553 ) Clingan, Councilor Davis, Councilor Hardt, Councilor McLaughlin, Councilor Sait, Councilor Scott, Councilor Strezo and Councilor Wheeler

- Supporting the Artificial Intelligence Civil Rights Act of 2025.

- Councilor Link stated that the request seeks to support federal legislation

regulating the use of artificial intelligence in consequential decisions affecting individuals’ lives, including those related to civil liberties, banking, and employment.

## RESULT: APPROVED

4.7. Resolution

By Councilor Link, Councilor Sait and Councilor Scott

(ID # 26-1554 ) Calling on the Mayor to adopt policies prohibiting city staff from using

artificial intelligence to generate public-facing media and prohibiting the replacement of city employees with artificial intelligence as detailed within. Councilor Link explained that the request seeks to establish a practical city policy on artificial intelligence (AI) use that prioritizes engaging local artists over AI-generated work whenever possible and prohibits replacing city staff

- with AI.

## RESULT: APPROVED

4.8. Resolution

By Councilor Mbah, Councilor Hardt and Councilor Link

(ID # 26-1530 ) That the Administration develop or update a written protocol for

severe-weather preparedness during construction and roof repair projects, including verification that roof drains are functioning properly, temporary

protective measures are in place, and responsible personnel are available to respond promptly to reports of water intrusion.

## RESULT: APPROVED

4.9. Resolution

By Councilor Wheeler, Councilor Hardt, Councilor Sait, Councilor Link, (ID # 26-1547 ) Councilor Clingan, Councilor McLaughlin and Councilor Mbah

Urging the state to protect Mass Save and clean energy grants.

## RESULT: APPROVED

4.10. Communication By Councilor Wheeler

(ID # 26-1548 ) Sharing the Metro Boston Homeland Security Region's (MBHSR) Urban

Area Security Initiative (UASI) fiscal year 2024 plan and allocations.

## RESULT: PLACED ON FILE AND SENT FOR DISCUSSION

FOLLOWUP: Finance Committee

4.11. Resolution

By Councilor Clingan

(ID # 26-1549 ) That the Director of Mobility install a "SLOW - CHILDREN CROSSING"

sign on Heath Street, close to the corner of Heath & Moreland Streets.

## RESULT: APPROVED

4.12. Resolution

By Councilor Hardt, Councilor Link and Councilor Mbah

(ID # 26-1552 ) Opposing the draft combined sewer overflows long-term control plan and calling for a regional solution.

- Councilor Hardt explained the purpose of the combined sewer overflow
- (CSO) system and noted that the City is legally required by the
- Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) and Department of Environmental

Protection (DEP) to develop a draft control plan. She expressed concerns about the limitations of the process, the significant costs involved, and the plan’s ability to keep pace with climate change. She described the issue as a technical approach to a political problem. The resolution calls for examining the root causes, building on existing efforts, exploring hybrid solutions that provide greater control, and advocating for additional state, regional, and federal funding.

- Councilor Wheeler raised concerns about financial inequities identified in

previous CSO presentations and stated that he could not support the resolution’s call for more costly solutions. Councilor McLaughlin

acknowledged the need for CSO improvements but expressed frustration with rising water and sewer rates despite previous assurances that rates

would stabilize following major infrastructure investments. He argued that addressing pollution in a state river should be a state or regional

- responsibility rather than falling primarily on the City.

Councilor Wheeler requested a roll call vote on the item.

## RESULT: APPROVED AYE:

- Ward Three City Councilor Ewen-Campen, City Councilor
- At Large Link, Ward Two City Councilor Scott, Ward Four
- City Councilor Clingan, Ward Five City Councilor Sait,
- Ward Seven City Councilor Hardt, Ward One City
- Councilor McLaughlin, City Councilor At Large Mbah, and
- Ward Six City Councilor Davis

## NAY:

- City Councilor At Large Wheeler
- ABSENT: City Councilor At Large Strezo

## 5. UNFINISHED BUSINESS

## 6. REPORTS OF COMMITTEES

6.A. FINANCE COMMITTEE

6.A.1. Committee Report Report of the Committee on Finance, meeting on October 20, 2026.

## (ID # 26-1568 )

Councilor Wheeler reported that the committee recommended approval of several items, including funding for the 2026 Community Grant Cycle, acceptance and expenditure of a $35,000 grant from the Massachusetts

Department of Mental Health, a reduction in the borrowing appropriation for the Poplar Street Project, and additional borrowing and appropriations for

the Poplar Street Pump Station. The committee also discussed Teen Center costs, artificial intelligence contracts, and bankruptcy-related financial

- matters concerning 808 Windsor Place.

## RESULT: APPROVED

6.A.2. Order

By Councilor Link and Councilor Wheeler

(ID # 26-1032 ) That the Director of Procurement and Contracting Services provide this City

Council with a report of all artificial intelligence vendors and services for which the city currently has contracts or ongoing payment obligations.

## RESULT: WORK COMPLETED

6.A.3. Mayor's Request Requesting approval to accept and expend a $35,000 grant with no new

(ID # 26-1414 ) match required, from the Mass Department of Mental Health to the Police

- Department for overtime/backfill to support officers and supervisors in
- obtaining/maintaining Crisis Intervention Team Training certification.

## RESULT: APPROVED

6.A.4. Order

By Councilor Mbah

(ID # 26-1429 ) That the Director of Finance and the Director of Economic Development

report to this Council on the situation of financial bankruptcy, involving the investor funds, holding equity in the empty lab building at 808 Windsor

- Place, Boynton Yards.

## RESULT: WORK COMPLETED

6.A.5. Mayor's Request Requesting approval to appropriate $100,000 from the Racial and Social

(ID # 26-1472 ) Justice Fund to implement the 2026 Community Grant Cycle.

## RESULT: APPROVED

6.A.6. Mayor's Request Requesting authorization to reduce the borrowing appropriation of (ID # 26-1486 ) $89,332,819 for the Poplar Street Project by $2,097,667.05.

## RESULT: APPROVED

6.A.7. Mayor's Request Requesting authorization to borrow $3,143,557 in a bond, and to appropriate

(ID # 26-1487 ) the same amount for additional costs of design, construction, and equipping

of the Poplar Street Pump Station.

## RESULT: APPROVED AYE:

- Ward Three City Councilor Ewen-Campen, City Councilor
- At Large Link, Ward Two City Councilor Scott, Ward Four
- City Councilor Clingan, Ward Five City Councilor Sait,
- City Councilor At Large Wheeler, Ward Seven City
- Councilor Hardt, Ward One City Councilor McLaughlin,
- City Councilor At Large Mbah, and Ward Six City
- Councilor Davis
- ABSENT: City Councilor At Large Strezo

6.B. LAND USE COMMITTEE

6.B.1. Committee Report Report of the Committee on Land Use, meeting on October 15, 2026.

## (ID # 26-1567 )

- Councilor Ewen-Campen reported that the committee discussed several

proposed zoning ordinance amendments, including changes to ground-story elevations, principal entrances, affordable housing terminology, and corrections to typographical errors. As the Planning Board has not yet issued its recommendations, the committee recommended laying the items on the table.

7.19. Mayor's

Conveying the Fiscal Year 2027-2031 Capital Investment Plan.

Communication

## (ID # 26-1556 )

- Mayor Wilson introduced the Capital Investment Plan, emphasizing its

focus on ongoing projects, infrastructure maintenance, and critical school and facility repairs while limiting new borrowing due to anticipated budget

- constraints.

- Budget Director Michael Mastrobuoni presented the plan, which includes

approximately $8.1 million in ongoing investments funded primarily through reserves and Community Preservation Act (CPA) funds. The plan

prioritizes fleet replacement, street and sidewalk improvements, fire apparatus, school repairs, and facility upgrades. He noted that future

borrowing capacity is limited by projected operating budget pressures and that several long-term priorities, including public safety infrastructure, decarbonization, fire station rehabilitation, and school improvements, remain unfunded. These projects will require additional financial planning, grants, or alternative funding sources before proceeding.

- Director of Infrastructure and Asset Management Richard Raiche was also
- available to address engineering and infrastructure-related questions.

## RESULT: PLACED ON FILE
